translationRepairs: Song: Wei Zi Qi, younger brother of King Zhou by a concubine. First enfeoffment.
Song: Wei Zi Qi, elder brother of King Zhou by a concubine. First enfeoffment.
In 宋微子啟，紂庶兄, 庶兄 means elder half-brother by a secondary consort; the before wrongly has younger brother, and the after restores that kinship correctly.
Song Wei Zi Qi, Zhou younger brother by concubine. First enfeoffed.
Song Wei Zi Qi, Zhou elder brother by concubine. First enfeoffed.
The same 庶兄 in s111 requires elder, not younger, in the literal field; the after correctly replaces younger with elder without other change.
Qi was born wise, Yao established him as Minister of Rites, and gave him the surname Zi.
Qi was born wise, Yao established him as Minister of the Multitudes (Situ), and gave him the surname Zi.
堯立為司徒 names the office 司徒 (Situ, Minister of the Multitudes), not rites; Minister of Rites would be 宗伯/禮官, so the after is the accurate rendering.
Qi born wise, Yao established as Minister of Rites, surnamed him Zi clan.
Qi born wise, Yao established as Minister of the Multitudes (Situ), surnamed him Zi clan.
Literal likewise mistranslates 司徒 as Minister of Rites; replacing with Minister of the Multitudes (Situ) matches the Chinese office title.
The cell is 熊黮; 黮 is read tán, so Xiong Tan is the correct English name and Xiong Meng mismatches the characters.
Literal repeats the same wrong Meng reading for 黮; Xiong Tan is the correct reading of 熊黮.
Speaking in terms of the Three Dynasties genealogical transmissions, Hou Ji had a father named Emperor Ku (Gaoxin);
Speaking in terms of the Three Dynasties genealogical transmissions, Hou Ji had a father named Gaoxin;
后稷有父名高辛 names only 高辛; Emperor Ku is an interpretive insertion absent from this unit, and the after keeps the source name alone.
Emperor Ku (Gaoxin) was the great-grandson of the Yellow Emperor.
Gaoxin was the great-grandson of the Yellow Emperor.
高辛，黃帝曾孫 likewise has only 高辛; stripping the inserted Emperor Ku restores the clause without changing the great-grandson claim.
子者茲 is immediately glossed as 茲，益大也, so 茲 here carries the 'increase' sense (滋), not demonstrative 'this'; the after matches that etymological gloss.
